limitations: No detector-rule catalog entry under the concern label is available, so the exact matcher implementation, taint sources, sanitizers, path sensitivity, and severity logic are unresolved.
The advisory is evidence for a disclosed historical pattern, not a universal semantic contract for all applications.
Absence of a locally visible validation call does not prove absence of validation in an interprocedural helper, configuration policy, receiving component, or server-mediated flow.
The finding message is a normalized advisory record, not runtime telemetry.
predicates: A URL-bearing value originates from an external Intent, deep-link-like input, or another untrusted source.
The value, including a Uri-derived serialization or transformation, reaches WebView.loadUrl(...) on the relevant path.
There is no evidence of an effective origin-validation policy for the loaded destination.
Where a navigation handler is part of the finding, content-originated navigation can reach shouldOverrideUrlLoading(...) and influence an application navigation sink.
JavaScript enablement is an aggravating configuration predicate only when it applies to the WebView that loads the influenced content.
detector_semantics.claim: The disclosed historical pattern consists of an Intent data URI copied into a JavaScript-enabled WebView load, with a WebView navigation handler that can forward a custom-scheme URL tail into application navigation.

unknowns: No published detector-rule catalog entry named WebViewUrlValidationSpec is available; its precise matcher semantics, taint model, sanitizer list, and reporting thresholds remain unresolved.
No API type named WebViewUrlValidationSpec is evidenced; the relevant APIs are Android Intent, Uri, WebView, WebSettings, WebViewClient, and WebResourceRequest.
The intended origin policy is unknown, including accepted schemes, exact hosts, ports, paths, redirect policy, custom-scheme policy, and subframe policy.
It is unknown whether validation occurs in omitted code, a called helper, a receiving activity or presenter, an application-wide navigation policy, or a server-side redirect endpoint.
It is unknown whether the initiating component is externally reachable in the analyzed build, whether the candidate URI passes Android intent resolution, or whether caller identity is checked.

It is unknown whether the navigation callback processes only main-frame navigations, whether it can receive untrusted iframe navigation, and whether a custom-scheme URL is attacker-reachable in the deployed WebView.
The advisory concerns a tested historical version and a later patched version; the analyzed artifact version, commit, Android API level, target SDK, and WebView implementation are not provided.

documented_behavior: Intent.getData() retrieves the data URI operated on by an Intent and can return null.
Uri.buildUpon() constructs a builder by copying the original Uri attributes, and Uri.toString() returns its encoded string representation.
WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled(true) enables JavaScript execution; the documented default is false.

WebViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, WebResourceRequest) allows the host application to take control of a URL about to load. It can be triggered by page JavaScript, user navigation, or HTTP redirects; true cancels the current load and false continues it.
WebResourceRequest.getUrl() returns the request URI, and isForMainFrame() identifies whether the request fetches the main-frame document.
preconditions: A WebView URL load must occur on the thread that created the WebView.
The URL argument to WebView.loadUrl(String) cannot be null.
Intent data must be non-null before code can transform or serialize it.
WebViewClient callback behavior depends on navigation type; app-initiated loadUrl navigation, POST requests, and some navigation classes have different callback behavior.
unknowns: The platform APIs do not define a single universal operation that proves a URL has passed a sufficient application-specific origin policy.
The required trusted-origin policy is application-specific: allowed schemes, exact authorities, ports, paths, redirects, custom schemes, and relevance of subframes are not determined by these APIs.
The observed APIs do not disclose whether loaded remote content is controlled by a trusted party.
The relevant Android System WebView implementation, target SDK, device API level, and installed WebView version are not provided.

events.condition: Observation: code reads an Intent action or data URI. Predicate satisfied only when the particular Intent data value is reachable from an external or otherwise untrusted sender; merely reading Intent data does not prove external control. Intent.getData() may return null.
events.name: external_intent_uri_observed

events.condition: Observation: a Uri is copied, parsed, serialized, or modified. Predicate satisfied only when the resulting URL retains attacker-controlled scheme, authority, path, query, or redirect-relevant data and flows to a WebView or navigation sink. Uri.buildUpon() alone is not origin validation.
events.name: uri_preservation_or_transformation_observed

events.condition: Observation: JavaScript is enabled in a WebSettings instance. Predicate satisfied only when those settings belong to the same WebView instance that loads the externally influenced URL at runtime.
events.name: javascript_enabled_for_webview_observed

events.condition: Observation: a WebView URL-load call is present. Predicate satisfied only when its argument is dataflow-derived from the external URI and no effective strict origin policy rejects disallowed scheme, host, port, path, and relevant redirect behavior before the call.
events.name: webview_url_load_observed

events.condition: Observation: a WebViewClient navigation callback is installed or overridden. Predicate satisfied only when navigation originating from content loaded in the relevant WebView can reach the callback and the callback makes a security-relevant routing decision without validating request origin or destination. The callback has documented limits: it is not invoked for app-initiated loadUrl navigation or POST requests, and it can receive subframe and non-HTTP(S) navigation.
events.name: navigation_callback_observed

events.condition: Observation: code recognizes a URL or custom-scheme prefix and forwards all or part of that value to an Activity, Intent, application route, or another WebView-related sink. Predicate satisfied only when the forwarded portion remains attacker-controlled and the receiver treats it as a URL, route, command, or other privileged input without an independent restrictive validation step.
events.name: custom_navigation_forwarding_observed

events.condition: Observation: code inspects a URL component or refers to an allowlist. Predicate satisfied only when validation parses the effective URL and enforces the intended policy on all relevant paths: expected scheme, exact host or authority, port where relevant, path constraints where relevant, and redirects or navigation-callback destinations. A scheme-only, substring, or prefix check is not sufficient evidence of origin validation.
events.name: origin_validation_evidence_observed

important_note: WebViewUrlValidationSpec is a concern label, not a published CrySL rule, detector-catalog rule, or governed API type. It describes the source-to-WebView and navigation-handler pattern evidenced by the historical advisory. It does not establish that every occurrence is exploitable, that an attacker can invoke the entry point, or that downstream navigation reaches a sensitive capability.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not invent a class, library API, CrySL rule, or detector-catalog entry named WebViewUrlValidationSpec.

Do not infer that an arbitrary third-party application can invoke the relevant component solely from a source-level Intent read; exported status, intent filters, permissions, caller identity checks, and platform resolution require evidence.
Do not infer that every URL passed to WebView.loadUrl(...) is network-reachable, attacker-hosted, or untrusted.
Do not infer that JavaScript is enabled for the same WebView instance and program point merely because setJavaScriptEnabled(true) appears elsewhere.
Do not infer that a WebViewClient callback is reached for the initial app-initiated loadUrl call, for POST navigation, or only for main-frame navigation.
Do not infer that a custom-scheme prefix check validates a trusted web origin.
Do not infer addJavascriptInterface, file access, cookie access, credential exposure, native-code execution, or a JavaScript bridge unless separately evidenced.
Do not infer that a vulnerability remains present in a current release from a historical advisory or normalized advisory record.
Do not infer that a report proves exploitability, impact, or a required repository change.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: A runtime exploit requires additional facts: an attacker must supply an accepted input URI; the affected path must execute; the WebView must load attacker-controlled or otherwise untrusted content; relevant navigation must reach the handler; and the forwarded destination or command must reach impactful application behavior. Android guidance recommends avoiding navigation to sites outside the application's control where possible and allowlisting loaded content.
security_semantics.detector_claim: Potential arbitrary or insufficiently validated URL loading is indicated when externally influenced URL data reaches a JavaScript-enabled WebView and a navigation callback can relay content-controlled navigation into application routing without established origin validation. The concern maps conceptually to CWE-346, which covers failure to verify a data or communication source and includes an Android WebView URL-scheme handling example.

compatibility: The WebResourceRequest overload is available from Android API level 21; WebViewClient documentation directs use of that overload on API level 24 and above.
Callback behavior must be tested against supported Android API levels and the Android System WebView implementation because shouldOverrideUrlLoading is not called for all navigation types.
Target SDK, device API level, installed WebView implementation, network-security configuration, and URI-resolution behavior must be recorded for compatibility conclusions.
If JavaScript interfaces, file URLs, or custom schemes are implicated, their platform-version-specific settings and defaults require separate evidence.
runtime: Test a candidate external Intent or equivalent untrusted URL input and confirm that the application accepts it.
Observe that the candidate URL is loaded in the intended WebView and that JavaScript is executable if claimed.
Observe redirect, script-initiated navigation, or user navigation reaching the installed WebViewClient callback.
Observe that the downstream receiver accepts an attacker-influenced route, URL, or command and produces the claimed security-relevant behavior.
Where impact involves sensitive data or native capability, obtain direct evidence of the relevant bridge, permissions, storage access, authentication state, or sensitive operation.
source_level: Establish complete interprocedural dataflow from the external URL-bearing source, through Uri/String conversions and helper calls, to the exact WebView.loadUrl(...) receiver.
Establish that the source is externally controllable or otherwise untrusted, including component export, intent-filter, permission, caller-validation, or deep-link dispatch facts as applicable.
Establish that JavaScript enablement, if an aggravating predicate, applies to the same WebView instance and path as the URL load.
For navigation-forwarding variants, establish that the callback URL derives from WebView navigation and that the forwarded URL tail or route parameter reaches the receiving sink.
Establish the presence or absence of an effective full-origin policy across relevant branches; isolated scheme, substring, or prefix checks are insufficient evidence of an allowlisted origin.

name: WebViewUrlValidationSpec
source_title: GHSL-2023-142: Arbitrary URL loading in a WebView in Home Assistant Android Companion — CVE-2023-41898
semantic_scope: For every finding of this concern, the detector observes a possible source-level flow in which externally supplied or insufficiently trusted URL-bearing input reaches an Android WebView load operation without evidence of a strict effective origin policy, optionally combined with JavaScript enablement and a WebViewClient navigation handler that can reinterpret or forward navigation URLs into application-controlled routing. This scope is control-flow and dataflow evidence, not proof of runtime reachability or exploitation.
known_false_positive_shapes: Intent data is reachable only from a signature-protected, permission-protected, explicit, or caller-authenticated path.
The URL is derived from an Intent but is replaced by a fixed trusted destination before the relevant WebView.loadUrl(...) call.
A strict origin allowlist exists in a helper, central navigation policy, configuration object, or receiving component but is not visible to local matching.
The JavaScript-enabled settings belong to a different WebView instance, are disabled before the influenced load, or execute only on an unreachable branch.
The apparent source-to-sink path is infeasible because of action, null, state, account, feature-flag, lifecycle, or server-response guards.
The navigation handler recognizes only fixed commands and never forwards an attacker-controlled suffix, path, URL, or route parameter.
The callback receives a request but the path is limited to a harmless subframe, non-main-frame resource, or a destination that cannot activate sensitive application behavior.
The reported code is from a version outside the analyzed artifact or was materially changed since the advisory-tested version.
protocol: externally supplied Intent data URI → Uri-derived URL string → JavaScript-enabled WebView.loadUrl(...) → WebView-initiated navigation → WebViewClient.shouldOverrideUrlLoading(...) → custom-scheme handling or application-navigation sink

detector_examples.message: External finding (CVE-2023-41898): MyActivity.onCreate loads Intent data into a JavaScript-enabled WebView without validating the origin. Navigation handling can forward an attacker-controlled URL into the main app WebView. Source tag: 2023.6.0. This is a normalized advisory record, not a runtime log.
